QF.id: VII Introduction to Securities Broking Operations_91

question.text: Trade allocation in back office operations for institutional trades refers to:

answer.text: Distributing a single institutional trade across sub-schemes or portfolios based on deal-sheet instructions
Deciding which exchange to route orders to
Setting price limits for each security
Hiring additional staff for the trading desk

explanation.text: The Logic: For institutional trades, back-office trade allocation is the process of distributing a single executed institutional trade across the relevant sub-schemes or portfolios based on the deal-sheet instructions received with the order. The Trap: Trade allocation is an operational distribution function, not order routing, price-limit setting, or staffing. Note: Pages 105-106 support back-office allocation of institutional trades to sub-schemes/portfolios; broader fair-allocation, cherry-picking and SEBI-monitoring claims are not stated in the pages checked.
